question: Should OpenClaw adopt this broad AI-safety taxonomy as a permanent core/plugin-SDK/operator surface, including durable operator retention, or keep the work outside core until a narrower owner-approved contract is defined?
rationale: The patch creates new public plugin, manifest, Gateway, CLI, exporter, and UI contracts; resolving its defects alone cannot decide the long-term taxonomy, authority model, data retention, and compatibility commitment.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core contract
options.body: Approve a bounded canonical event and retention model, then require the branch to forward manifest authority, use authoritative session IDs, and add approved persistent storage.

options.title: Keep diagnostics extension-owned
options.body: Decline the new core/plugin-SDK contract and pursue optional safety reporting through existing diagnostics plugin seams until a concrete core API gap is established.

options.title: Pause pending design review
options.body: Leave the PR open but pause implementation until security, plugin, and observability owners agree on taxonomy, provenance, and retention guarantees.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed core contract
recommendation.body: Approve a bounded canonical event and retention model, then require the branch to forward manifest authority, use authoritative session IDs, and add approved persistent storage.

likelyOwner.reason: skoya has authored the complete proposed series and can supply the needed design context, though a separate repository decision owner should sponsor any permanent public contract.
